# R318 — Numerical and model-quality acceptance for inference-kernel changes

Date: 2026-10-13 (JST). Read-only audit for updated Xe/current optimized-kernel acceptance. No tests, imports, builds, inference, GPU/profiler/process operation, Git operation, cleanup, or source edits were performed. The current decode receipt was not read. This report proposes measurement criteria; it does not approve a kernel or judge any current output.

## Decision

Do not require byte-identical generated text across inference implementations as the general quality gate. Free-running generation is a discontinuous comparison: a small logit change near a top-two tie can choose a different token, which changes every later input and recurrent state. Different generated IDs prove that the implementations are not bitwise/greedy-output equivalent on that run; alone, they do not show a quality regression. The closed b9 diagnostic in R316 (same 32K prompt, first eight output IDs equal, ninth differs, LP5 differs, normal exit/no reported runtime fault) is therefore a divergence signal for follow-up, not pass/fail evidence of quality.

Use three separate acceptance layers: (1) exact microfixtures for arithmetic-preserving kernel contracts; (2) fixed-history numerical comparisons for production logits/state; and (3) held-out end-task quality metrics with predeclared, task-appropriate margins. Track operational/runtime success independently. Performance is a fourth measurement and must not be traded against quality implicitly.

## Compact acceptance protocol

**A/A calibration first.** Run the unchanged baseline repeatedly under the same device, binary, compiler/runtime, weights, prompt, fixed token history, cache/routing and launch settings intended for A/B. This measures repeat-to-repeat variation in logits, NLL, KL and task scores. Keep all runs; report the distribution and source of variation. For nondeterministic generation, repeat free-running A/A too, but do not substitute its output agreement rate for teacher-forced numerical measurements. The variation estimate is calibration, not an allowance for nonfinite values, wrong tensor shapes, missing tokens, memory/queue faults or a failed runtime status.

**Fixed token histories (same tokenizer IDs and contexts).** Evaluate baseline and candidate on exactly the same prompt and continuation IDs, including at least the 32K+ production histories relevant to the optimization. Use one isolated quality capture path and separately timed quiet runs. Align every prediction row with its absolute position and target ID; require full requested position coverage, matching history hashes, correct context/chunk route, finite logits and complete run status. At each position compare:

- full-vocabulary raw logits: max absolute and relative error, RMS error and distribution of errors; include top-1/top-2 IDs, top-two margin, rank of the fixed target, and top-K overlap;
- normalized full-vocabulary probabilities: forward and reverse KL (state direction), optionally Jensen–Shannon, plus per-position and aggregate summaries/quantiles;
- fixed-target token log-probability/NLL, mean NLL and derived perplexity across the same corpus (with the same BOS, masking, context window and tokenization); retain per-position paired NLL deltas, not only one aggregate;
- recurrent/model state checks at a small number of agreed boundaries when a state representation is available, to localize a divergence before it amplifies.

Use stable log-sum-exp and accumulate metrics in higher precision. Full KL requires full-vocabulary rows from both implementations; top-K logprobs cannot recover tail mass, so call top-K-only metrics “top-K overlap/score,” never full KL. Hash raw rows and put them under an explicit consumer/byte budget; retain a compact table and delete captures after verification unless an unresolved numerical question requires them.

A fixed-history test asks whether candidate distributions score the *same* histories similarly. It does not ask whether free-running generated continuations must be identical. If exact logits/greedy IDs are a requirement for a particular deterministic route, specify that separately as an implementation contract and only for that route/build/device.

**End-task quality.** Run a small, locked, representative set of held-out tasks matching intended use (for example code completion/unit-tested code, instruction following, factual recall, and math only if users rely on it). Freeze dataset revision, examples, prompt/chat template, tools, sampling, stop rules, answer extraction and grader; use paired examples for baseline/candidate and preserve per-example outputs and score deltas. Report accuracy/pass@1 or task-specific rubric, invalid/refusal/format rates, and uncertainty intervals (paired bootstrap or exact binomial intervals as appropriate), plus aggregate results. Use enough examples to resolve the chosen non-inferiority margin; a handful of generations or one 16-token output is diagnostic only. Choose task set and margins from product requirements and baseline uncertainty before seeing candidate outcomes. There is no universal acceptable KL, NLL, PPL, top-1 agreement or accuracy delta.

This is consistent with established evaluation interfaces that distinguish `loglikelihood` (fixed continuation score) from `generate_until` (free generation) and rolling likelihood/perplexity [EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness model guide](https://github.com/EleutherAI/lm-evaluation-harness/blob/main/docs/model_guide.md). llama.cpp uses both corpus perplexity and logits-file-based KL comparison for quantization evaluation and warns that full logits artifacts can be large [llama.cpp model-conversion/perplexity guide](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/examples/model-conversion/README.md). SGLang similarly documents separate accuracy evaluation such as GSM8K/MMLU rather than treating throughput as accuracy [SGLang evaluation examples](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/docs/cookbook/autoregressive/Qwen/Qwen3.5.mdx). These provide measurement patterns, not cutoffs transferable to Strata or Qwen3.8.

**Arithmetic-preserving microfixtures.** Keep a small deterministic fixture for the candidate kernel's declared contract: fixed small tensors/quantized blocks, exact layouts/strides/tails, CPU or scalar reference, boundary and rejected-geometry cases, and output/status checks. Require bitwise parity only when the optimized implementation claims to preserve the same arithmetic, ordering, and rounding semantics. If it changes reduction order, fused operations, quantized approximation or intermediate precision, record this as a changed numerical algorithm and compare with tolerances established from the reference's own repeat noise and product error budget. Microfixture parity proves that kernel primitive on covered inputs; it does not prove model quality.

## Acceptance and failure interpretation

Before A/B, write down a product-level non-inferiority rule for each selected task metric and the analysis population; base it on repeat A/A variation, evaluation sample size and user consequence. A candidate may pass despite changed generated strings if fixed-history metrics and end-task quality remain within those predeclared bounds and runtime correctness passes. A candidate may fail despite identical short greedy output if distribution/NLL or representative task quality regresses materially.

Report categories separately:

- **Numerical parity:** exact or close values for specified fixed histories and kernel fixtures.
- **Quality non-inferiority:** task scores meet the declared bound with uncertainty accounted for.
- **Behavioral reproducibility:** same-route same-seed free-run text agreement, if desired; informational unless explicitly required.
- **Operational correctness:** process completes normally; required outputs/positions are present; all outputs are finite; no sanitizer/queue/device/kernel fault, OOM, or invalid state transition. Any such failure is a hard operational failure, not something A/A noise or quality tolerance can waive.
- **Performance:** separate paired timing results on the same admitted route and workload. Do not infer performance from quality captures or compare timings across unlike routes.

Intel's own compiler guide treats accuracy, reproducibility and performance as distinct objectives with tradeoffs and notes that compiler floating-point modes can change math behavior [Intel DPC++ floating-point tradeoffs](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/dpcpp-cpp-compiler/developer-guide-reference/2026-0/programming-tradeoffs-floating-point-applications.html). Its oneMKL reproducibility guarantees are explicitly limited to specified routines and conditions [oneMKL reproducibility conditions](https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/docs/onemkl/developer-guide-linux/2024-2/reproducibility-conditions.html); that is another reason not to universalize a bitwise requirement across distinct runtimes/devices/kernels. A vLLM test uses `assert_close` tolerances for selected logprob comparisons to a Hugging Face reference, but those are test-specific values, not an endorsed universal threshold for this model/device [vLLM logprob tests](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/tests/v1/sample/test_logprobs.py).

## Existing harness coverage in W

The current curated worktree `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012` contains a reusable *method example*, not a production-ready current-kernel acceptance harness:

- `bench/results/2026-09-27-esp/esp_kl.py` consumes fixed `.ids`, invokes baseline/variant in separate arms, loads full-vocabulary float32 logits, computes stable log-softmax/KL, top-1 agreement and target-token perplexity. Its README/result reports 2,557 fixed tokens. It is a valuable reference implementation for metrics and paired fixed histories, but it uses an older Windows standalone token-by-token path and unrelated projection experiment. It does not establish a 32K+ current Xe production route, output-quality acceptance, runtime fault certification or an application-task benchmark.
- `bench/results/2026-09-30-xe-iq3xxs/window_logits.py` and `compare_greedy.py` compare limited logits/free-running candidates, but do not give the full production fixed-continuation scoring/held-out task protocol requested here.
- R316 says current b9 status is a single diagnostic with a 16-token free-running suffix, no numerical equivalence result. R336 says the public `--serve`/`--dump-logits`/`--spec-follow` interface on the audited revision is not a persistent token-forcing full-distribution decode interface. R297 documents that `STRATA_LOGPOS` is limited to `read_windows` and does not score a long batched Prefill continuation; `STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS` captures only the first post-prompt distribution. These reports are revision-specific; confirm the exact current source/build hook before using it.

Thus the likely reusable pieces are the `esp_kl.py` metric calculations, fixed-ID fixtures and comparator patterns, and standard task-evaluation frameworks. The missing piece is a verified current-production hook/harness that scores every reference continuation token on the actual updated Xe/current optimized-kernel state without changing the timed route. If that needs implementation, build the opt-in scoring path separately from a quiet perf binary/run and gate it on exact position/target coverage and A/A self-consistency. Existing code/artifacts were only inspected; no test or inference was run.

## Minimum ledger fields

Record source/build and model/weight/tokenizer hashes; device, driver, runtime, compiler and flags; exact prompt/continuation ID hashes and absolute positions; expert formats and selected kernel/routes; context, KV, cache, PLE and prefill settings; sampling/eval configuration; A/A repeats; per-position numerical summaries and paired NLL; task datasets/revisions/seed/prompt templates/grader/paired outcomes; confidence intervals and predeclared margin; output/runtime/fault/exit status; performance run IDs and clean timing separately. Keep no raw logits after paired metrics are validated unless an identified consumer still needs them.

## Prior evidence and limits

Reviewed R316 (`research-xe-b9-numerical-route-divergence-round316-v1.txt`), R336 (`round336-native-decode-teacherforce-existing-interface-contract.txt`), R297 (`round297-compiled-generator-quality-hook-provenance-correction.txt`), R204 (`research-intermediate-fp16-bf16-quality-evidence-transfer-contract-round204-v1.txt`), R258 (`research-native-cache-rounding-vs-dm16-quality-controls-round258-v1.txt`), the W scripts above, and primary upstream evaluation/numerics sources. This is an acceptance-method proposal only. It neither declares the current candidate good/bad nor creates a universal numeric threshold.
